note: Festival-wide (not per-project) visitor guide data referenced by the chatbot assistant. Unconfirmed items are left as "Not available yet" — update this file once confirmed, no code change or redeploy needed.

food.saleLocations: There is no single food court — food and drinks are sold individually by each project/booth that offers them, at that project's own location.
food.eatableRestAreas: There are eating areas on the 1st floor (near CS/Room 125, just past the middle gate) and on the 3rd floor (next to the library).

restrooms: 1st floor: one men's and one women's restroom in the Hall, and one men's and one women's restroom in the Classroom Building. 2nd floor: men's and women's restrooms in the Classroom Building, plus one additional women's restroom in the Main Building. 3rd floor: men's and women's restrooms in the Classroom Building. Accessible (multipurpose) restrooms are available on every floor.
infoDesk: The student council's information desk is at the 1F entrance (map no. 22, same place as stroller safekeeping). Detail page: https://mif-2026.studio.site/en/detail/1-22
nurseOffice: Please direct anyone who is injured or feeling unwell to the nurse's office on the 1st floor. If it seems urgent, also alert a nearby teacher or staff member.

access.walkTime: About a 5-minute walk from Youga Station's east exit to the school.
access.note: Please do not drop off or pick up by car near the school, and please do not park or leave bicycles at nearby shops.

lostAndFound: For lost items, please ask at classroom "MP2", right next to the entry/exit gate on the 1st floor. Lost tickets cannot be reissued; if asked about a lost ticket, say it cannot be reissued.
notices: Information on this site is updated regularly. Please check for the latest details before visiting.
Event details may change or be cancelled without notice.
If you are injured or feel unwell, please go to the nurse's office on the 1st floor.
Please bring athletic shoes if you plan to join a sports club experience activity.
Outdoor experience activities will be cancelled in case of rain.
Please refrain from visiting if you have a fever, cough, or other symptoms.
Photography on campus is limited to our students, their guardians, teachers, and contracted photographers.
Even those listed above should refrain from photography except at designated photo spots.
Please do not drop off or pick up by car near the school.
Please do not park or leave bicycles at nearby shops.
ticketRules: This is separate from the performance tickets. For performance projects, give the ticket info on each project's own page.

Groups that use these tickets are all projects except food, sales, performances and club activities. Concretely: grade projects other than the J1 presentation and the physical expression performance, all volunteer-group projects, and the basic seminar projects.
If a project is not crowded, tickets are not used and visitors can enter directly.

Among the seminars, those led by Mr. Nagasaki and Mr. Ichikawa hand out tickets from the morning. J2 grade projects start handing out tickets once the crowd overflows, and stop when the tickets run out.
Until about 10 people are waiting, visitors simply line up without tickets. Once about 10 people are waiting, the project switches to handing out tickets.
Each ticket shows a return time slot. Slots are :00-:15 or :30-:45 of an hour. Visitors leave and come back in that slot. The 9 o'clock hour only has :30-:45, and the last hour has only :00-:15.
People arriving after ticket distribution has started receive a ticket instead of joining the line.
A latecomer can still enter while it is the same hour as the ticket's slot. For example a 10:30-10:45 ticket works until 10:59 and becomes invalid from 11:00.
When nobody with a ticket is waiting, visitors may be told they can go in right away.
Whether one ticket covers a group or one person differs by project. Tell visitors to check at each project's reception.
Each visitor must collect their own ticket. Collecting for several people, swapping for another time slot, and returning a ticket are not allowed.
A visitor without a ticket generally cannot enter together with a friend who has one. If the project is empty and needs no waiting, the group may allow it.
Stepping out of the line briefly is fine as long as at least one person stays. If your turn comes while you are away, the person behind goes first.
glossary: MSTC is a group of students who do research activities year-round. They present at the MSTC Research Presentation and the MSTC Representatives' Presentation.
ZERO to ONE is the name for the research-presentation projects with map numbers Z1 and Z2. Z1 is the MSTC Research Presentation and Z2 is the Basic Seminar and Basic Research Presentation.
J1 to J3 are junior high years 1 to 3, and S1 to S3 are high school years 1 to 3. A trailing letter is the class.

messages.title: Junior High School Principal's Message
messages.text: "Every single student is wonderful!" These are words that many visitors come up to me and share during every MIF. While I am delighted by how many people say this, what surprises me even more each time is the remarkably wide range of ages represented among them. Creating a school festival that can bring smiles to everyone, from young children to senior citizens, may sound simple, but it is actually quite difficult. Perhaps it is something that can only be achieved by MITA students, who embrace diversity and welcome people from all walks of life. "Eclipse" is, in a sense, a show of light and shadow. The many successes and failures our students have experienced on their journey toward this event will surely give rise to, and communicate, something that touches the hearts and stirs the imagination of our many visitors. We sincerely hope that you will join us and enjoy the "show of light and shadow" unfolding throughout every corner of our school. As we prepare for the 2026 MIF, we have received tremendous support from the PTA, the Chigusa Association, and the Supporters' Association from the planning stages onward. We would like to express our heartfelt gratitude to everyone involved.

messages.title: Senior High School Principal's Message
messages.text: The theme "Eclipse" brings to mind Jun'ichiro Tanizaki, who found charm and beauty precisely within the shadows. By turning our thoughts to the unseen and the hidden, our imagination expands vastly, giving rise to new forms of beauty and value that have never existed before. I look forward to seeing each of you use your creative freedom to generate new and beautiful scenery found nowhere else; at the same time, I hope that MIF, including the entire process leading up to this moment, serves as "a wonderful place filled with smiles", and a space where we can truly experience and reflect upon our "daily lives" and "reality." To the members of the Chigusa-kai, the Supporters' Association, and the PTA: thank you for your continued support. We hope that all our visitors will enjoy seeing the energetic students of MITA International School of Science and sharing a delightful time of intergenerational interaction.

messages.title: MIF Executive Committee Chairperson's Message
messages.text: This year's MIF theme is "Eclipse". Just as a solar or lunar eclipse occurs when celestial bodies align for a single extraordinary moment, MIF can only come to life when many people come together toward one shared goal. The MIF Committee, participating students, teachers, parents, and many others have spent months preparing for these two special days. We hope that everyone who visits will experience the energy of this moment and feel the passion that each student has put into making MIF possible. Please enjoy our one and only "Eclipse."

sections.title: Admission & entry tickets (admission tickets; separate from project crowd-control tickets)
lines: MIF is a fully reservation-based event. People without a reservation or ticket cannot enter.
Elementary school students considering junior high entrance exams and their guardians must reserve in advance. Guardians alone cannot enter. Reservation details: https://www.mita-is.ed.jp/news/2623/
General visitors need an invitation ticket.
The Pop Dance Club performance requires a separate viewing ticket. Prospective students should apply for the set that includes the viewing ticket when reserving entry.
The exact location of the entry/exit gates and the on-the-day reception procedure: no information.

sections.title: Allergies and payment methods
lines: Ingredients and allergy information are not in this data or the project list, including the cafeteria. Items and prices are in 'Items on sale and prices'.

For allergy questions, say it is not listed, attach the detail-page URL of the relevant project, and tell visitors to go to the project's location and ask the staff directly. Never state that something is safe or free of an allergen.
Payment is cashless only. Charging on campus is not available. Cash cannot be used.

Accepted: contactless credit cards (Visa, Mastercard, American Express, JCB, Diners Club, Discover), transit IC cards (Kitaca, Suica, PASMO, TOICA, manaca, ICOCA, SUGOCA, nimoca, Hayakaken), QUICPay, d Barai, Rakuten Pay (R Pay) and iD.

Tell visitors this applies to all projects including the cafeteria; per-project exceptions: no information. The official site top page also has a 'Payment Methods' section near the bottom (https://mif-2026.studio.site/en).

sections.title: Performance / stage locations
lines: A performance project's location follows the floor, building and map number on its list line. Performances in the Hall building on 1F take place in the main hall mentioned in their descriptions.
When asked where a stage or performance is, always attach the project's detail-page URL and the venue-map link, not just the place name.

sections.title: Nearest restroom
lines: When asked for the nearest restroom to a project or room, call the nearest_restroom tool and give all three types when the visitor did not specify one, or only the requested type, using the nearby project names as landmarks. The distance is how close it looks on the map, not walking distance, so say 'closest on the map' and add the venue-map link (https://mif-2026.studio.site/en/maps). Never mention staff-only or teacher restrooms or anything not in the data. Accessible restrooms exist on every floor.
